The narrative pass (Phase 79): every changed line, before and after

Phase 79 judged every player-facing line against a four-point rubric and rewrote only the lines that failed it. A line that passed stays word for word. This page lists every line that changed, grouped by where the player reads it, with the event it describes and why it changed.

How to read this page

  • Before is the line at the phase base (commit cd560cc8). After is the line the game prints now.
  • An Oracle or rail line is one representative rendering of its builder, from a fixed synthetic event, so its numbers and names are examples. “…” stands for a value filled in at play time.
  • new line means nothing was printed there before. removed means the line is gone, and the why says what replaced it.
  • Why lists every plan that changed the line, in order, with its reasons.
  • Ledgers read: 79-02, 79-02c, 79-03, 79-04, 79-05, 79-06, 79-07, 79-08, 79-09, 79-10, 79-11, 79-12, 88-01, 88-04, 89-02, q-260927-opf, q-260927-rsx, q-260928-frz, q-260928-tsx, q-260928-z-sq2, q-260928-z2-cos, q-260928-z3-hrs, q-260928-z4-nrf, q-260928-z5-bug.

How to ask for changes

Quote the line (or its key, the code in the first column) and the tone you want instead. Every tone change goes into one quick follow-up task, not a new phase.

The rubric

  1. States what happened, to whom and with what result (numbers where the player needs them).
  2. Reads naturally aloud, with no stilted or translated-sounding phrasing.
  3. The deadpan, family-friendly joke comes AFTER the fact, never instead of it.
  4. Is accurate to what the engine actually did, so the narration never contradicts the event.

The standing rulings

  • HP, not WP: no player-facing string says "wp" or "WP".
  • Roll-high everywhere (ROLL-04): a higher face is always better; a fixed die states its range ("only on 18–20"), a die that scales with level speaks in faces ("only your die's top face lands").
  • U+2212 for a minus and U+2013 for a range: "−4 hp", "18–20".
  • Dungeon Master and Game Master, never "Maze Master".
  • Family-friendly deadpan: no profanity, gore or adult content; the darkness is in the wit, not the shock. A Pilfer's text never names a diagnosis.
  • House spelling is British (79-12): "armour", "honour", "rumour"; item names such as the Cloak of Armor keep their spelling.
  • A dismissible card is for decisions and big updates; a minor event is a rail line with its narrative sentence.

bank:CLASS_NOTE.FighterHero tab dossier, Class section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)The best Hit Points in the book, any armour you can lift, and a 5 to hit — which at skill level I still means three swings in four hit nothing but corridor. Fighters are the only delvers who die of something other than a mistake. A scroll, for you, is an intelligence roll that can backfire — unless you paid for Runes/Signs.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04), honest number): “a 5 to hit” is roll-under phrasing for a die that scales with level; now “your top five faces to hit”, with the level-1 d20 range 16–20 pinned to facesRangeText(CLASSES.Fighter.toHit, 20). The three-in-four joke is kept and pinned.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04), honest number): “a 3 to hit — six swings in seven” was roll-under and a loose ratio; now “only your top three faces to hit — 18–20 on the d20 at skill level I, so seventeen swings in twenty are decorative”, every number pinned to CLASSES['Magic User'].toHit.

bank:RACE_NOTE.DwarvenHero tab dossier, Race section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Two extra damage, a wilmst a day to feed, and every creature down here swings at you like it has been practising — but your armour shrugs off wear at half the rate everyone else's does, and being small makes you one face harder to hit besides. Built low, built cheap, built to be hit, built to keep the dents. Dwarves call this a fair trade. Dwarves are rarely asked.Two extra damage, a single Hit Point a night when the rations run out, and every creature down here swings at you like it has been practising — but your armour shrugs off wear at half the rate everyone else's does, and being small makes you one face harder to hit besides. Built low, built cheap, built to be hit, built to keep the dents. Dwarves call this a fair trade. Dwarves are rarely asked.

79-03 (accurate to the engine, what happened, to whom): “a wilmst a day to feed” stated a gold cost that no rule charges; the Dwarven upkeep is 1 HP on a night without rations (a Human's is 4). Only that clause changed; the fair-trade joke stays.

bank:RACE_NOTE.ElvenHero tab dossier, Race section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Thin-boned, easy to hit, and carrying not much more than half a person's Hit Points — but you strike a die better than anyone has a right to, and hit on a 5 whatever the class. Small costs you two points of damage and nothing else; the size rule has nothing left to add to how thin-boned or easy to hit you already were. The elven plan is to kill it before it notices how little you can take. The plan holds until it doesn't.Thin-boned, easy to hit, and carrying not much more than half a person's Hit Points — but you strike a die better than anyone has a right to, and your top five faces land whatever the class. Small costs you two points of damage and nothing else; the size rule has nothing left to add to how thin-boned or easy to hit you already were. The elven plan is to kill it before it notices how little you can take. The plan holds until it doesn't.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04), accurate to the engine): “hit on a 5” read as a single low face under the roll-high engine; the Elven floor is a count of winning faces (RACES.Elven.toHit = 5), so it now says “your top five faces land”. The joke and the size clause stay.

bank:SUB_NOTE.AcrobatHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Everything needs a 3 to lay a hand on you and you may carry nothing but a knife. You strike with it like a fighter — nobody armours against a dagger held by someone who will not stand still.Nothing lays a hand on you except on its top four faces, and you may carry nothing but a knife. You strike with it like a fighter — nobody armours against a dagger held by someone who will not stand still.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04)): “Everything needs a 3 to lay a hand on you” was roll-under; foes land on only their top three faces against an Acrobat (foeToHitVs = 3).

q-260928-z4-nrf (what happened, to whom, accurate to the engine): User ruling 2026-09-28 ("Acrobat: foes hit on top 4"): foes land on an Acrobat with their top four faces, not three (foeToHitVs = 4). The blurb states the new number.

bank:SUB_NOTE.Bardthe sub-class blurb (roller and Hero tab)Five songs, one every hundred squares, and dragons hand over gifts to hear them. Camp for the night and creatures too stupid to know better come looking twice as often, and once the fighting starts they come for you first — which, down here, is most of them.Five songs, one every hundred squares, and every Human in here will at least hear you out before swinging. Camp for the night and creatures too stupid to know better come looking twice as often, and once the fighting starts they come for you first — which, down here, is most of them.

79-12 (accurate to the engine): Nothing in the engine has dragons give a Bard gifts; the Bard's real edge is that every Human will parley, which the line now states.

bank:SUB_NOTE.ClericHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Healing, turning the dead, chain mail and a shield: the one Magic User the dungeon cannot simply push over. A 4 to hit instead of a 3. The gods have rounded up.Healing, turning the dead, chain mail and a shield: the one Magic User the dungeon cannot simply push over. Your top four faces hit instead of three. The gods have rounded up.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04)): “A 4 to hit instead of a 3” was roll-under; a Cleric's top four faces hit instead of a Magic User's three (classNeed).

bank:SUB_NOTE.Con ArtistHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)You talk first, and anything with wit of 6 or under simply declines to fight you. Your first landed blow does no damage at all, because part of you is still hoping to sell them something.You talk first, and any level-one foe declines to fight you two times in three. Your first landed blow does no damage at all, because part of you is still hoping to sell them something.

79-03 (accurate to the engine, roll-high (ROLL-04)): “anything with wit of 6 or under simply declines to fight you” was wrong on both counts: the rule is a level-one foe leaving on four faces of a d6. Now “any level-one foe declines to fight you two times in three”.

bank:SUB_NOTE.GuardHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)No critical strike, ever, and three damage off the top until level four — but every creature down here needs one better than usual to land a blow on you. You are a professional. The profession is standing there.No critical strike, ever, and three damage off every blow at level one, one less each level until it is gone at four — but every creature down here lands on one face fewer against you. You are a professional. The profession is standing there.

79-03 (roll-high (ROLL-04), accurate to the engine, honest number): “needs one better” was roll-under, and “three damage off the top until level four” hid that the penalty shrinks each level; now it says three off at level one, one less each level, gone at four, and foes land on one face fewer. Pinned to weaponDamage and foeToHitVs.

bank:SUB_NOTE.Master of ArmsHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Plus two with every weapon ever forged, plus three with anything you have repaired yourself. You cannot parley — you attack creatures without question, literally — and once a fight has your scent there is no clean exit in round one either. The book files this under abilities.Plus two with every weapon ever forged, and every night in camp you hammer the dents out of your own armour. You cannot parley — you attack creatures without question, literally — and once a fight has your scent there is no clean exit in round one either. The book files this under abilities.

79-03 (accurate to the engine): “plus three with anything you have repaired yourself” is not a rule; what the engine does is patch the Master of Arms' own armour every night in camp (d6+3), so the clause says that.

bank:SUB_NOTE.NinjaHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)You never speak — literally; no fluency, no encounter, ever talks you out of a fight. The silence isn't a vow, it's a tactic.You never speak — literally; no fluency, no encounter, ever talks you out of a fight. Your opening strike lands for maximum damage and after that your top two faces open something up. The silence isn't a vow, it's a tactic.

bank:SUB_NOTE.Pilferthe sub-class blurb (roller and Hero tab)Traps disarm themselves in your presence and no sealed room has ever held you. Your hands, though, can't leave a magic ring, amulet, cloak or staff alone — use one and, about one time in twenty, it comes apart right there for a d10 of your own hp and is dust. Potions and scrolls you handle like anyone else.

79-12 (accurate to the engine): A Pilfer's fumble covers staves as well as rings, amulets and cloaks (PILFER_FUMBLE_KINDS), and the footer already said so; the prose now agrees.

bank:SUB_NOTE.SorcererHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)Two dozen spells to start and two more each level, nearly all of it fire, with a one-in-eight chance per level of simply forgetting the ones that aren't. bank:SUB_NOTE.SummonerHero tab dossier, Subclass section (heroTab.js#renderHeroTab)You can call something up from your very first day. It now says its own healing spells heal at half strength (the 2026-09-25 ruling that replaced the offense gate), and that the day-one summon is the small one, since only the full Summon is doubled and can backfire.
